title: Using Cell-substrate Impedance and Live Cell Imaging to Measure Real-time Changes in Cellular Adhesion and De-adhesion Induced by Matrix Modification
protocol: Culture bovine aortic endothelial cells on gelatin-coated tissue culture flasks in EGM-2 media.
Coat tissue culture surface with 0.1% w/v gelatin in PBS at RT for 15 min.
Harvest near-confluent cells by treating them with 0.05% w/v trypsin / 0.02% w/v EDTA in PBS at 37 °C.
Add complete EGM-2 media to quench the trypsin after cell detachment.
Centrifuge harvested cells (100 x g, 5 min).
Wash harvested cells once with serum-free Medium 199 containing 1% w/v bovine serum albumin (BSA).
Re-centrifuge washed cells (100 x g, 5 min).
Resuspend cells in serum-free Medium 199 containing 1% w/v BSA at 2.5 x 10^5 cells/ml or 5 x 10^5 cells/ml.
Maintain resuspended cells at 37 °C prior to use.
Coat fibronectin onto 96-well gold cell-substrate impedance microelectrode arrays.
Add 80 μl/well of purified bovine fibronectin at 5 μg/ml in PBS.
Incubate for 2 hr at 37 °C and remove the solution.
Incubate fibronectin-coated surfaces with MPO to allow the binding of MPO to the surface bound fibronectin.
Add 80 μl/well of purified human neutrophil MPO at 20 nM in Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS).
Incubate for 0.5 hr at 37 °C.
Wash surfaces twice with HBSS to remove any unbound MPO.
Add H2O2 (0-10 μM final concentration) to wells of the microelectrode array plate containing 80 μl/well HBSS.
Incubate for another 0.5 hr at 37 °C.
Add relevant inhibitors or modulators of MPO-catalyzed reactions to HBSS immediately prior to H2O2 addition.
Incubate for 0.5 hours after adding H2O2.
Add 10 mM methionine in 80 μl HBSS per well and incubate for 10 min at 37°C.
Block surfaces with BSA by adding 80 μl/well of BSA at 0.2% w/v in PBS, then incubate for 2 hours at 37°C.
Remove the solution after blocking.
Wash surfaces twice with HBSS.

Seed suspended endothelial cells by adding 200 μl/well of cells prepared in serum-free Medium 199 containing 1% BSA at a concentration of approximately 2.5 x 10^5 cells/ml onto native or MPO-oxidized fibronectin coated surfaces immediately after seeding.
Mount the microelectrode array plate onto the incubator port housed in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2 immediately after seeding cells.
Take a ‘blank’ reading using the instrument software to normalize subsequent cell index values.
Initiate acquisition of continuous cell index data, with at least one reading per minute.
Incubate cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2 hours.
Observe a plateauing of cell index values indicating maximal cell attachment and spreading.
Coat fibronectin onto 96-well gold microelectrode arrays by adding 80 μl/well of fibronectin at 5 μg/ml in PBS and incubating for 2 hr at 37 °C.
Block surfaces with BSA by adding BSA at 0.2% w/v in PBS, as indicated in 3.1, and incubate for 2 hr at 37 °C.
Incubate surfaces with MPO to allow binding of MPO to fibronectin by adding 20 nM purified human MPO in HBSS at the volumes indicated in 3.1 and incubating for 0.5 hr at 37 °C.
Wash surfaces twice with HBSS to remove unbound MPO.
Coat fibronectin onto 35 mm glass-bottomed cell culture dishes by adding 2 ml/dish of fibronectin at 5 μg/ml in PBS and incubating for 2 hr at 37 °C.
Block surfaces with BSA as described previously.
Incubate surfaces with MPO to allow binding, as described previously.
Wash surfaces twice with HBSS to remove unbound MPO.

Seed suspended endothelial cells onto native or MPO-bearing fibronectin-coated surfaces by adding 200 μl/well at 2.5 x 10^5 cells/ml to 96-well microelectrode arrays and 2 ml/dish at 5 x 10^5 cells/ml to 35 mm glass-bottomed dishes.

Mount 96 well microelectrode array plates onto the cell-substrate impedance incubator port housed in a 37 °C incubator with 5% CO2 and take ‘blank’ readings to initiate continuous acquisition of cell index data.
Transfer 35 mm glass-bottomed cell culture dishes to a 37 °C incubator with 5% CO2.
Incubate cells at 37 °C for 2 hr to allow maximal cell attachment and spreading.
Briefly remove the 96 well microelectrode array plate from the 37 °C incubator.
Pause cell index readings at this point.
Remove cell supernatant.
Add warmed (37 °C) HBSS as per step 3.1.
Place the microelectrode array plate back into the 37 °C incubator port.
Re-commence cell index readings at this point.
Allow cells to equilibrate in the HBSS for 0.5 hr.
Initiate MPO-catalyzed, HOCl-dependent fibronectin oxidation and de-adhesion.
Remove the microelectrode array plate from the incubator and pause cell index measurements.
Add H2O2 to the HBSS to achieve a final concentration of 0-10 μM.
Gently mix by repeated pipetting.
Re-mount the microelectrode array back onto the 37 °C incubator port.
Re-commence the acquisition of cell index readings.
Remove the culture dish from the incubator and mount it onto a 37 °C heated stage of an inverted confocal microscope equipped with a 63X water objective lens and suitable DIC optics.
Focus on cells and optimize DIC optics (Köhler illumination, bias retardation and camera offset/gain).
Initiate DIC movie and record baseline readings of untreated cells for 1 min.
Add H2O2 to the culture dish to achieve a final concentration of 0-10 μM.
Gently mix by repeated pipetting.
Re-focus the microscope if necessary.
Continue recording DIC movies of the treated cells for the required time period.
Open DIC live cell imaging movies recorded immediately prior to and after the initiation of MPO-mediated fibronectin oxidation in an image analysis program.
Select multiple cells randomly from at least two separate DIC movies and measure their projected area in sequential frames by manually tracing their membrane edge.
Quantify the number of enclosed pixels for each cell's projected area.
Export raw data (projected cell area versus time) to an Excel spreadsheet.
Normalize cell area data by setting values recorded immediately prior to MPO-mediated fibronectin oxidation at a value of 1.
Present data as a plot of normalized cell area (y-axis) versus time (x-axis).
